description: The village composed (core src/editor/layout/composition/village.ts, composeVillage): G1's network laid on the plan, then G2/G12, G5, G3/G6, G9, G7 and G8 over what each step left. These cases pin the hand-offs between the rules, which each rule's own file does not: a lane is a route for the props and the lanterns, a post keeps off what G2, G5, G3 and the engine's stairs stood, the feet's undergrowth keeps off it, a seat moves with its bench and a villager works at its prop where G2 stood it. Authored in core. Plan frame: IR (x, z) metres.

sources.fixturesFrom: conformance/layout/ground-plan.json (copied byte for byte; the corpus test guards the copy)

cases.name: village: Brightwater Vale composed whole, on its terrain
cases.note: Brightwater's followed plan on its terrain, its seven doors, its settled houses by archetype, its 85 dressing props and its seven lanterns, composed in one call: the same inputs as the network, yards, grouping and lantern files' Brightwater cases, now handed from step to step.

cases.name: village: a lane G1 lays is a route for G9's lantern and G2's bench, and G3's feet keep off it
cases.note: One lot set back 15.45 m from a road: G1 lays a lane from its gate to the road and a door path to the gate, superseding the lot's old footpath. The lantern 1.75 m off the lane (8 m off the road) stands beside the lane; the bench 3.95 m off the lane regroups at the lane, and its seat goes with it; the far bench has no anchor within 20 m and is set aside, so its sitter stands; the crate regroups at the house and its worker is drawn in to it there; the tree's foot plants skip the spots on the lane. An idler stands 0.1 m inside bench.far's disc: G2 sets that bench aside, so it is not stood and the idler is left where it is.

cases.name: village: with no lane laid, the lantern is loose and the bench regroups at the door path
cases.note: The same village with the street join cut to 10 m (ruleOverrides): the gate is 15.45 m from the road, so no lane is laid and the lot is unjoined. The lantern, 8 m from the road and far from the door path, is loose (the door path is the one route G1 still lays); the bench regroups at the door path instead, and the tree's foot plants stand where the lane would be. The control for the case above: what the lane decides. An idler stands 0.1 m inside bench.far's disc: G2 sets that bench aside, so it is not stood and the idler is left where it is.

cases.name: village: G9's posts keep off the props G2 stood and the porch decks G5 laid, not off the props G2 set aside
cases.note: No building within 20 m of the crate: G2 sets it aside, so it is not stood and lantern.crate stands at its nearest spot (10, 2.5), 0.1 m from where the crate was. The bench ties to the road and stands, so lantern.bench's nearest spot (-10, 2.5), 0.1 m from its disc, is refused and the post steps 0.5 m forward along the road. The house's door faces the road; lantern.door's nearest spot beside the door path is on G5's porch deck, so it steps out along the path past the deck.

cases.name: village: a gate on the square: its lane of no length is no route, and the lanterns go to the square's edge
cases.note: network.json's 'plaza: a gate on a plaza joins it where it stands' with its house and two lanterns in the square. G1 lays a lane of no length at the gate, which G9 does not take as a route: lamp, 0.82 m from the gate, goes to the square's edge, stepping along it off the door path's mouth, and far stands 0.5 m inside the square's nearest edge (9.5, 12). Neither stands on the open floor (B9 round 4's B1).

cases.name: village: a bench regrouped at a house takes its back to the wall (m4)
cases.note: One 8 m square house at the origin and nothing else on the plan: no lot, no road. A bench 5.4 m off its east wall, its input heading 1.2 rad, is 2.1 m past the tie reach and is regrouped at the wall; its heading is replaced by the one away from the wall's nearest point (0: east), so its back is to the house and its slots run along the wall, and its sitter sits on it facing that way. The house-anchor half of regroupedHeading (a route anchor faces the route: the lane cases).

cases.name: village: G9's posts keep off G5's yard items and edge runs, G3's trees and G4's stairs (m1)
cases.note: The G9 case's house, its hedged home lot (front at z = 9) and road.main, plus road.east 1.8 m off the lot's east side, a short open path inside the yard 1.4 m below its washline, a tree by road.main and a 0.5 m stair the engine stood by it. lantern.item's nearest spot beside the yard path (-21, 17.6) is 0.4 m from G5's washline at (-21, 18), inside its nominal 0.5 m disc (YARD_ITEM_RADIUS_M), and so is the one 0.5 m back; past the path's end there is no station, so the post goes across the path to (-21, 15.6). lantern.hedge's spot beside road.east (-20.1, 12) is 0.2 m from the hedge's east run (x = -20.3), and every station along that run is too; the post goes across the road to (-16.1, 12). lantern.tree's spot (0, 2.5) is 0.2 m from the trunk of the tree G3 keeps at (0.2, 2.5) (a 0.25 m trunk), so it steps back to (-0.5, 2.5); lantern.sapling's (30, 2.5) is as near the trunk of the sapling G3 keeps at (30.2, 2.5) and steps back to (29.5, 2.5); lantern.stair's (20, 2.5) is inside the stair's disc and the post steps to (21, 2.5). Without these obstacles every post would stand at its nearest spot (the test reruns G9 without them).

cases.name: village: a back door's path goes round its own house and through the gate's gap (m2)
cases.note: network.json's back-door lot composed whole: its road, its lot (front at z = 5), its house from z = 8 to 13 and a back door at (-1, 13) facing away from the road. composeVillage hands G1 the buildings' outlines, so the door path goes round the house's west side, the shorter way, by (-4, 14) and (-4, 7), and through the approach (0, 6.3) on the gate's axis and out square through the gap; without the outlines it would run straight from (-1, 14) to the gate across the house (network.json's control).
